Title: Fact checking Trump's recent claims about the economy

Summary: 
The article examines President Trump’s recent economic claims against data released in 2025. It notes that consumer confidence fell to its lowest level since May, yet the U.S. economy grew at a 3.8% pace in Q2 2025. Trump’s assertions about falling energy and grocery prices are contradicted by federal statistics: residential electricity costs rose 6.2% in August 2025 versus a year earlier, and natural gas prices increased 13.8% (U.S. Energy Information Administration). The average household energy cost climbed from $263.44 in August 2024 to $282.84 in August 2025. Trump’s promise to cut electricity prices by half within 12–18 months is unsupported by current trends, which forecast a 18% rise in residential rates over the next few years. Gasoline prices fell from $3.52 to $3.30 per gallon between August 2024 and August 2025, but overall gas prices have remained flat since Trump took office, with a 3.21 average at the start of his term. Grocery prices have risen 0.6% in August 2025, the fastest monthly increase in nearly three years, and 2.7% from August 2024 to August 2025 (Bureau of Labor Statistics). A pound of ground beef rose from $5.55 to $6.32, and ground coffee from $7.02 to $8.87, while egg prices fell from $4.95 to $3.59 per dozen. Strain of the American Enterprise Institute notes that grocery inflation is still above the overall CPI, which rose 1.3% since January. Mortgage rates fell from 7.04% on Jan. 16 to 6.26% on Sept. 18, yet affordability remains low. Trump’s claim that inflation has been defeated is challenged by Strain, who cites a 2.9% CPI rise in August and that inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target. The article also reports that the S&P 500 and Dow Jones have reached all‑time highs during Trump’s second term, and that U.S. factory production rose 0.9% YoY in August, though manufacturing jobs fell 12,000. Blue‑collar wage growth increased 1.7% in the first five months of Trump’s term, while white‑collar growth lagged inflation. Overall, the piece presents data that largely contradicts Trump’s optimistic narrative.
